cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: Large regions of the Universe may hold less dark energy than average, and it could show up in local expansion
cards.stage_headline: Stage 1 of 5: an idea, not yet tested.
cards.stage_note: A phenomenological model with numerical predictions. No data fit yet. Not peer reviewed; the authors invite comments.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: Dark energy would stop being uniform, and patches of it could feed into the Hubble tension.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: In their model, a 10% deficiency slows a typical void’s expansion by about 2.7%, leaving 60–100 km/s velocity residuals across 30–50 Mpc.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Whether any survey sees those residuals. The H0 effect needs deficiencies of about 20% across several hundred Mpc.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: DESI, Rubin or peculiar-velocity surveys find the predicted residuals in voids, beyond what matter alone explains.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: The authors flag isotropy and dynamical-consistency limits; surveys that find no residuals would rule it out.

cards.todo: No outreach yet. Set a citation alert and watch for void or peculiar-velocity analyses that test it.
cards.rule_text: a survey reports velocity residuals in voids of the predicted size.
cards.compare_text: An earlier analysis found a local underdensity of matter does not resolve the Hubble tension.

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: The basic feeling of being conscious starts in the brainstem, not the cortex
cards.people: Marshall Devor, Mark Baron · The Neuroscientist
cards.stage_headline: Stage 1 of 5: an idea, not yet tested.
cards.stage_note: A hypothesis paper built on existing findings. We read the press release, not the paper.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: Moves the search for consciousness away from the cortex, where the leading theories place it.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: It draws on pain research, brain stimulation, injury cases where cortical damage spares pain, and anesthesia circuits.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Any explicit, numbered predictions. The release points only to the mesopontine tegmentum as a place to test it.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: Experiments on mesopontine tegmentum circuits change conscious experience while the cortex is left intact.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Conscious experience persists when those brainstem circuits are disabled.

follow.name: Mark Baron
follow.role: Hebrew University and Harvard Medical School

cards.todo: Get the full paper and list any predictions it makes that a cortical theory would not.
cards.rule_text: a brainstem experiment designed to separate it from cortical theories.
cards.compare_text: The Cogitate adversarial collaboration (Nature, 2025) challenged key predictions of both leading cortical theories.

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: The Galileo Project plans a passive-radar observatory to image and take spectra of UAP
cards.stage_note: Install target within about a year. Loeb says it is funded but hasn’t named backers.
cards.impact_heading: IF IT WORKS, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: Civilian, high-resolution images and spectra of unidentified objects, the data UAP claims usually lack.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Passive radar uses reflections of existing signals to steer a metre-class telescope. It would be the fourth observatory, in Ithaca, after Massachusetts, Pennsylvania and Nevada.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Budget, backers, and whether the imaging will be good enough. No findings have been announced.

follow.name: Avi Loeb
follow.role: Harvard, director of the Galileo Project

cards.todo: No outreach yet. When the observatory is commissioned, ask whether its raw data will be public.
cards.compare_text: The UAP FILES critique below, and Breakthrough Listen’s 3I/ATLAS search, which found no credible signal down to about 0.1 W.

cards.label: CRITIQUE
cards.claim: The former head of the Pentagon’s UAP office says the disclosure movement rests on recycled cases and circular reporting
cards.people: Sean Kirkpatrick, interviewed by Zach Weissmueller
cards.stage_note: It rests on the 2024 AARO report Kirkpatrick wrote.
cards.impact_text: It is the only pushback in this week’s set, and it bears on every UAP item we cover.

details.heading: What he says
details.text: Some widely shared videos were already resolved but were reissued as unresolved. No official review has confirmed a UAP as extraterrestrial technology.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: He is a party to the dispute, and he contests accounts by David Grusch and Luis Elizondo.

follow.name: Sean Kirkpatrick
follow.role: former head of AARO, the Pentagon’s UAP office

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.claim: NASA’s technosignature database finds 112 search approaches, and none of the 28 tried is complete
cards.people: Nick Siegler (NASA JPL), Eddie Schwieterman, Evan Sneed (UC Riverside)
cards.stage_note: First shown at IAUS404 in March; this write-up is from Nov 8.
cards.impact_text: A map of which searches are feasible but untried, which is where funding would add the most.

details.heading: What it holds
details.text: 41 technosignatures, 112 approaches (61% doable from the ground), each scored on Sofia Sheikh’s nine axes of merit.

details.heading: What’s next
details.text: Planned hosting with the NASA Exoplanet Archive at Caltech’s IPAC, plus an AI agent that flags new papers.

follow.name: Nick Siegler
follow.role: Chief Technologist, NASA Exoplanet Exploration Program, JPL

follow.name: Sofia Sheikh
follow.role: SETI Institute, author of the axes of merit
